column1: Context: Use this checklist during testing. Mark each item Pass / Fail / N/A and capture evidence for any failure.

column2: Requirement / Criterion
column3: Expected behavior
column4: Pass / Fail criteria

column2: Controls can be identified without vision
column3: Buttons/knobs are distinguishable by shape, spacing, tactile marking, text, speech, or equivalent app support.
column4: Pass if a user can locate and distinguish core controls without relying only on sight.

column2: Controls operate without excessive force or fine motor precision
column3: Core controls do not require tight grasping, pinching, twisting, sustained pressure, or simultaneous actions without an alternative.
column4: Fail if important actions require excessive force, precision, or timed multi-button input.

column2: Controls can be explored safely
column3: Touch exploration does not trigger unwanted activation, or an equivalent accessible method exists.
column4: Fail if tactile exploration activates controls or causes accidental changes.

column2: Selected cycle and settings are perceivable
column3: Cycle, temperature, spin, lock status, and remaining time are readable and/or available non-visually.
column4: Fail if required settings or status are visual-only.

column2: Labels and states are readable
column3: Text, icons, and active states have sufficient contrast and are visible from expected standing/seated positions.
column4: Fail if text/states are unreadable because of contrast, glare, size, or angle.

column2: Color is not the only indicator
column3: Selection, warnings, and errors use text, icons, patterns, position, speech, or other redundant cues.
column4: Fail if color alone communicates state or error information.

column2: Essential audio has an alternative
column3: Completion tones, warning beeps, and spoken output have visual, tactile, or app-based equivalents.
column4: Fail if essential information is sound-only.

column2: Audio is controllable when used for access
column3: Volume can be adjusted and users can review repeated speech or alerts when provided.
column4: Fail if speech/alerts cannot be controlled or reviewed.

column2: A non-visual path exists for core use
column3: A user can power on, choose a common cycle, adjust key settings, start, monitor, and identify completion without relying only on vision.
column4: Fail if core operation depends on visual-only cues and no equivalent accessible path exists.

column2: Touchscreen or touch panel has an accessible alternative
column3: If a touchscreen is used, users can complete core tasks with speech output, accessible app equivalence, or a non-touch alternative.
column4: Fail if touchscreen-only operation blocks independent use.

column2: Errors are identified clearly
column3: Errors are provided in plain language or understandable equivalents, not only codes, lights, colors, or beeps.
column4: Fail if the user cannot identify the problem.

column2: Recovery steps are available
column3: The product explains how to recover from common errors and lets users review the message again if needed.
column4: Fail if recovery is missing, ambiguous, or not accessible.

column2: Consumable compartments are identifiable
column3: Detergent/softener/bleach areas use clear text, tactile differentiation, shape, or an accessible equivalent.
column4: Fail if compartments rely only on icons, color, or position.

column2: Instructions avoid sensory-only wording
column3: Instructions do not rely only on phrases such as “press the red light” or “use the left icon.”
column4: Fail if users need color, shape, or location alone to follow instructions.

column2: Documentation is accessible
column3: Required manuals/help/error references are available in accessible formats and explain accessibility-relevant features.
column4: Fail if required documentation is inaccessible or missing key operational guidance.

column2: Maintenance alerts are accessible
column3: Cleaning/filter/drum-care prompts are presented in accessible, understandable formats.
column4: Fail if reminders are visual-only, sound-only, or unexplained.

column2: Maintenance access is operable
column3: Routine consumer maintenance areas can be identified and opened without excessive force or unsafe posture.
column4: Fail if expected maintenance tasks are not independently operable.

column2: Controls expose accessible names and states
column3: Screen readers identify labels, roles, values, and selected states correctly.
column4: Fail if controls are unlabeled or status is not exposed.

column2: Status and errors are announced
column3: Pairing, start/pause, errors, completion, and remaining time are announced or reviewable accessibly.
column4: Fail if updates are visual-only.

column2: Large text and contrast are supported
column3: Text scales without clipping/loss and UI components maintain usable contrast.
column4: Fail if large text causes truncation, overlap, or loss of controls.

column2: Required technology provides equivalent access
column3: If an app/voice assistant is required for consumers with disabilities, it provides equivalent control, status, and error access.
column4: Fail if required technology is incomplete, inaccessible, or adds unequal burden.

column2: Core controls are within accessible reach
column3: Controls needed for core operation, such as power, cycle selection, settings, start/pause, cancel, and lock controls, can be reached from expected standing and seated positions in the intended installation configuration.
column4: Pass if users can reach and operate core controls without unsafe posture, excessive stretching, obstruction, or repositioning the appliance. Fail if core controls are too high, too low, too deep, blocked, or only reachable with unsafe or excessive effort.

column2: Displays and status indicators are viewable from expected positions
column3: Displays, selected states, alerts, and progress indicators can be viewed from expected standing and seated positions without glare, obstruction, or extreme viewing angle.
column4: Pass if users can perceive important visual information from expected positions. Fail if users must stand, bend, lean, or move into an unsafe position to see required information.

column2: Loading and routine-use areas are reachable
column3: The door/lid, drum opening, detergent drawer, auto-dose tank, and other routine-use areas can be reached in the intended installation configuration.
column4: Pass if users can complete routine tasks such as loading laundry and adding detergent without unsafe posture, excessive reach, or obstruction. Fail if required areas are not reachable or require unsafe bending, stretching, or lifting.

column2: Maintenance areas are reachable when maintenance is consumer-performed
column3: Consumer maintenance areas, such as filter access, drain access, detergent drawer removal, or drum-clean controls, can be reached and approached safely.
column4: Pass if expected maintenance tasks can be reached and attempted from a safe position. Fail if maintenance areas are inaccessible due to height, depth, obstruction, floor-level placement without an alternative, or unsafe posture.

column1: - Record each checklist item as Pass, Fail, or N/A. Use N/A only when the item does not apply to the product or scoped test path.

- Recommended impact levels for prioritization: Critical (blocks core independent use or safe recovery), Major (serious barrier with workaround or partial alternative), Moderate (meaningful barrier affecting efficiency or understanding), Minor (secondary issue that reduces clarity/consistency).
